Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ggmira 1.0.0 (2026-11-19)

  • Fixed browser access on Windows (#36).
  • Fixed buttons in the browser (#35).
  • Smaller package: only the images used by MiRA’s app are bundled (#34).
  • Bundled MiRA 1.2; in RStudio’s Viewer pane the top bar now shows only the lab logo, leaving room for the plot (#33); removed the small-window warning.

ggmira 0.9.0 (2026-11-15)

The first release. ggmira draws multilayer networks in MiRA, the browser-based multilayer network visualizer, with a ggplot2-like syntax: start from a network with mira() and add components with +.

  • Elements: mira_node(), mira_intralayer(), mira_interlayer() and mira_layer() map colors and sizes to the data’s attributes, or set constants, shapes and names. Bipartite networks take settings per node set.
  • Scales: color_scale, color_values, color_palette, color_reverse and color_limits in each element (?mira_scales).
  • Layout, camera and legends: mira_layout(), mira_camera(), mira_legends().
  • Filters: mira_filter() draws only some nodes, links or layers.
  • Views: the plot can open in any of MiRA’s views: mira_mode_grid(), mira_mode_map(), mira_mode_layer(), mira_mode_meta(), mira_mode_dashboard(), mira_mode_data().
  • Files: mira_save() saves a plot as a PNG, JPG or PDF file, without opening a window.
  • Back to R: MiRA’s R button gives the ggmira code for the view on screen, changes made in MiRA included.
  • Help: mira_options() lists what each component can be set to for a network; mira_spec() shows what a plot sends to MiRA.
  • Opening: in the browser or in RStudio’s Viewer pane (print(p, viewer = TRUE)); plot_mira() opens a network with MiRA’s defaults.
  • Feedback: mira_feedback() and the documentation’s Feedback buttons open a filled-in GitHub issue.
  • MiRA: bundles MiRA 1.2, with one later change: in RStudio’s Viewer pane, MiRA’s top bar keeps only the lab logo, leaving room for the plot.
